We estimate that we will incur severance and termination costs of approximately $1.0 million in connection with the October 2026 RIF, which we expect to recognize during the quarter ending December 31, 2026, and we expect the October 2026 RIF to reduce our annual salary and benefits costs by approximately $3.2 million.
We plan to incorporate interim assessments of fasedienol's effect using eDiaries and qualitative patient surveys in the future Phase 3 study design, and to submit a revised protocol to the FDA.

Additionally, consistent with FDA feedback and recognition of fasedienol’s reported safety profile, we plan to focus future Phase 3 development of fasedienol on the overall treatment of SAD (not only acute treatment of SAD) for the general SAD population.

As of May 31, 2026, we estimate that the fasedienol clinical development program now exceeds ICH E1 minimum recommendations with over 1,500 subjects receiving at least a single exposure to fasedienol, over 300 subjects with at least 6-months of exposure, and over 100 subjects with at least 12 months of exposure.

We have an open IND for itruvone in the U.S. and plan to pursue Phase 2 clinical development of itruvone in the U.S. for the treatment of MDD, in an effort to build on the positive results from the previous exploratory Phase 2A clinical trial of itruvone in MDD described above.
AV-101 (4-Cl-KYN) is our oral prodrug candidate that targets the NMDAR (N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor), an ionotropic glutamate receptor in the brain.
We do not anticipate further development and commercialization of AV-101 on our own.

Research and development expenses continued to decrease as a result of these cash preservation measures and the conclusion of our current Phase 3 PALISADE-4 trial and Repeat Dose Study and we expect them to decrease further as a result of the October 2026 RIF, partially offset by severance and termination costs of approximately $1.0 million expected to be recognized during the quarter ending December 31, 2026.

We anticipate decreases in future research and development expenses although the extent will depend on our ability to secure funding for and initiate a further Phase 3 trial for fasedienol with the LSAS as the primary endpoint.

At this time, we cannot accurately estimate or know the nature, timing and costs of the efforts that will be necessary to complete the nonclinical and clinical development of any pherine product candidates we are developing or may develop.
We expect general and administrative expenses to remain at current levels as a result of our cash preservation measures after the results of PALISADE-3, and our March 2026 reduction in force.
